messages.author: b5953aeb62350bf5
messages.subject: suitability from rsf.fit
parts:
Hi Chris,

I'm trying to create a habitat prediction from rsf.fit objects using the suitability function. My code is: 

SUIT <- ctmm::suitability(cilla,
                              rsf = cilla.rsf,
                              R = rlist,
                              na.rm = TRUE,
                              grid = elev)

Where cilla is an animal in my as.telemetry object, cilla.rsf is the corresponding rsf, and rlist is my named list of rasters. 

When I run this I get an error: 
"Error in if (to == from) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed"

I assume the grid argument specifies a template for the suitability output, which I've specified as my elevation raster. Is that correct? Is there something I've coded incorrectly here?

Many thanks!

parts:
Thanks Chris, 

I was reading my rasters in as SpatRasters, using Terra, and it seems that was the problem. In that example I think I was also incorrectly trying to create a prediction for each animal by including my telemetry object along with the rsf.fit object. Re-running it as: 

SUIT <- ctmm::suitability(period.mean,

R = rlist,
                              na.rm = TRUE,
                              grid = elev)

Seems to be working, albeit slowly.

As I think I understand it, I should take the mean of all my rsf.fit objects (50 or so animals for a given year) and feed that into suitability() with my rlist. Is that correct?

Thanks!

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: [ctmm-user] Re: suitability from rsf.fit
parts:
Hi Ryan,

suitability() calculated from the mean() RSF would correspond to the suitability of the mean animal, while averaging the individual suitabilities would correspond to the mean suitability of the population. The two calculations are not the same unless the population variance is very low.

Right now I'm working on including the uncertainty in the suitability() output. After that, I could put together a mean suitability function if people want that.

Best,
Chris
